mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate signals a loosening of monetary policy, which typically leads to increased liquidity in the market and higher S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS decreases by >0.25% in the last month
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances when FEDFUNDS decreases by >0.25%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate indicates a weakening economy, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases by >0.5% in the last month
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances when UNRATE increases by >0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts suggests a strengthening economy, which leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances when HOUST increases.

failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances when INDPRO decreases by >1%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP combined with a decrease in unemployment rate signals a robust economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases by >1% and UNRATE decreases by >0.5% in the last quarter
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances when GDPC1 increases by >1% and UNRATE decreases by >0.5%.
